recommendation: Keep the commit. Because source/oids.ini is the permanent OID record and its header calls for FHIR product director review, a human reviewer should specifically confirm the registry update; future terminology content changes should remain in THO/Gender Harmony artifacts rather than core.
issue_request: FHIR-39219 was a Published FHIR-core PA issue resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It objected to discriminatory Sex for Clinical Use wording and approved renaming the concept to Sex Parameter for Clinical Use, updating the extension definition/name, and relying on the Gender Harmony IG for fuller guidance.
initial_application: Core commits 7a59cfb6be and 996823f8d5 renamed the local SFCU terminology and aligned the Patient example. Commit f3c0d3659c then moved Gender Harmony terminology out of core. Current Patient source already uses SPCU and the THO CodeSystem, but source/oids.ini still recorded the old sex-for-clinical-use URLs for the assigned OIDs.
additional_context: The FHIR Extension Pack contains the patient-sexParameterForClinicalUse extension with the approved title/description, and current THO hl7.terminology 6.5.0 publishes the sex-parameter-for-clinical-use CodeSystem and ValueSet with the same OIDs. Gender Harmony and PA minutes confirm most explanatory text was intentionally moved to GHIG. FHIR-39220 through FHIR-39225 are duplicate/background comments in the same SFCU/SPCU concern family.
reconciliation: Changed source/oids.ini so the active ValueSet OID entry and the commented external CodeSystem OID entry point to sex-parameter-for-clinical-use instead of sex-for-clinical-use. No Patient narrative, example, extension, or terminology definition change was needed.
source_changes: source/oids.ini: updated the SPCU ValueSet OID URL and commented CodeSystem OID URL from sex-for-clinical-use to sex-parameter-for-clinical-use.
